references.text: Describes the creation of heaven and earth, which Genesis 2:1 summarizes by stating that the work was completed.
Explicitly states that the Lord created heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them in six days—a direct parallel to the completion of creation in Gen 2:1.
Mentions that God created heaven, the heaven of heavens, and all their host, the earth, and everything on it—a direct parallel to the wording in Gen 2:1.
Speaks of how God's word created heaven and all its host, directly relevant to the creation account summarized in Gen 2:1.
Calls on everything in heaven to praise the Lord, who created them by His word, in line with the completion of creation in Gen 2:1.
Urges one to lift up their eyes and see who has created the host of heaven (צְבָא), directly relevant to 'all their host' in Gen 2:1.
Refers to God's works being finished from the foundation of the world, citing that God rested on the seventh day—directly linked to the completion of creation in Gen 2:1.
Psalm 33:6 confirms that the 'host' in Genesis 2:1 was created by God's word and links the completion to the mechanism of the act of creation.
A clear allusion where Isaiah confirms that the 'host' in Genesis 2:1 was created by God's command.
A direct allusion confirming that the completion in 2:1 included God's rest on the seventh day.
